assertions.name: mp_path_and_f64_path_are_now_the_same_convention
assertions.source: |z - z_mp()| = 4.10029e-18 (float64 epsilon scale) while the pre-migration mp value differed from the f64 one by 22.7044 %. Both halves are asserted: the gap is closed now, AND it was genuinely open before -- so this cannot pass by the two paths having always agreed.

assertions.name: gram_matrix_mp_agrees_with_G_as_its_docstring_claims
assertions.source: max |G_f64 - gram_matrix_mp()| = 2.08297e-16, against the docstring's '~1e-15'. Pre-migration this was 0.172 -- the claim was false while the module straddled conventions, and is restored by the migration rather than merely re-asserted.

assertions.name: lu_solve_fails_SILENTLY_on_the_singular_D_gram_at_every_precision
assertions.source: swept 20/50/120 dps: lu_solve RETURNED at every precision with max|x| = 6.46904e+20, 2.9117e+50, 1.47013e+120 and a visibly nonzero residual (~1e-3), never raising. This is why the convention swap could not be one line -- and why 'it would raise, so we would notice' is the wrong lesson.

assertions.name: quotient_solve_is_sane_where_lu_solve_is_not
assertions.source: gram_quotient_solve_mp on the identity NF: max|x| = 0.901221 (lu_solve gave 2.9117e+50), residual against the reachable part 1.67048e-51, minimum-norm (x . radical = 1.46167e-51), and it returns the radical component 0.472689 rather than hiding it. gram_inverse_mp() raises: True.

assertions.name: sdp_probe_premise_G_invertible_is_FALSE_under_D_for_both_anchors
assertions.source: qbeta_braid_nf_sdp_offset_probe states 'Since G is invertible (rank 6), G x = nf fixes x* uniquely'. Under D both anchors carry a radical component of 46.18 % (muon) and 47.26 % (proton) of their NF norm, so G x = nf is UNSATISFIABLE for both. The question is ill-posed under D, not merely harder; this probe deliberately does not re-solve it on the quotient and report an angle.

description: pyhecke.gram carried a convention straddle inside one module: the float64 z moved to convention D on 2026-08-15 while the mpmath mirror (z_mp, tr_m_mp, gram_matrix_mp) stayed on C, 22.70 % apart, with both docstrings asserting lockstep and gram_matrix_mp claiming a ~1e-15 agreement with G whose true gap was 0.172. The C spelling was the detector-blind 1/(sqrt(q)+1/sqrt(q)) = sqrt(q)/(q+1) catalogued in PR #5124. Migrated to D, float64-free. It is NOT a one-line swap: under D the mp Gram is exactly singular and mp.lu_solve does not raise -- swept 20..120 dps it returned max|x| ~ 10^dps with residual ~1e-3 at every precision, the mpmath analogue of the numpy behaviour that blocked this migration originally. Adds the float64-free quotient API mirroring the f64 side: radical_mp (the proved q-antisymmetriser), gram_quotient_solve_mp (minimum-norm solve on H_3(q)/rad, returning the unreachable radical component rather than hiding it), and gram_inverse_mp (raises, like gram_inverse). SEPARATE FINDING, not repaired: qbeta_braid_nf_sdp_offset_probe assumes G is invertible (rank 6); under D both its anchors carry a 47 % radical component, so G x = nf is UNSATISFIABLE and its question is ill-posed -- re-solving on the quotient and reporting an angle would launder that. NOT RUN: the 19 witness-emitting downstream producers whose committed values are C-frame and all move; that is a scoped bulk sweep. No value wired, no tier moved.
